11.meaning: I will cast, throw, or hurl — to fling something, or to place/put it down with force or deliberateness.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern, 'to cast / throw,' fronted by sa- ('will / shall'), which places the action in the near future. The u- prefix marks an 'I' subject. The final long '-ī' belongs to the weak (final-yāʾ) root of this verb, giving the first-person form 'I will cast.'
11.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter; (causative) to throw, cast, deliver

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: Hearts — the inner organ understood as the seat of feeling, intention, understanding, and faith. 'Qulūb' is the plural of 'qalb' (heart).
13.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the -i ending, the genitive case — which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the hearts') or follows a preposition ('in the hearts').
13.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; the heart, that which fluctuates and turns

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

16.meaning: Terror, dread, intense fear — overwhelming fright that grips and unsettles a person. 'Ruʿb' is a fear that fills and shakes the heart.
16.grammar: A noun ('terror') with the -a ending, marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb ('… the terror'). With 'al-' ('the') it is definite. The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-ruʿba).
16.root: ر-ع-ب (r-ʿ-b) — to fill with dread, to terrify

17.meaning: A command addressed to a group meaning 'strike!' or 'hit!' — with the prefixed particle giving the sense 'so/then strike', presenting the action as a consequence or result of something prior.
17.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The fa- prefix marks a result or sequence ('so', 'then'). The -ū ending is the plural masculine command marker, addressing several people: 'you all do it'. The written initial alif (اضۡ) is a connecting alif (hamzat al-waṣl) carrying a kasra, added as a vocalic prop because the imperative stem begins with a consonant cluster that could not otherwise be pronounced — nothing is dropped; this helping vowel is prefixed.
17.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, to beat; also figuratively to set forth (an example) or to travel

18.meaning: 'Above / over / on top of.' An adverb of place meaning the higher position relative to something else; it can also mean 'superior to' or 'beyond.'
18.grammar: An adverb of place that is normally attached to a following noun ('above …'). Its fixed -a ending is the form such place-words take when they govern the noun that follows them.
18.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, surpass, exceed

19.meaning: The necks — the plural of the neck, the part joining head to body.
19.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the necks'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the necks') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The form aʿnāq is a broken (irregular internal) plural of the singular ʿunuq.

20.meaning: A command addressed to a group meaning 'and strike!' or 'and hit!' — joining this command to a preceding one.
20.grammar: An imperative (command) verb joined by the connective wa- ('and'). The -ū ending is the plural masculine command marker, addressing several people: 'you all do it'. The written initial alif (اضۡ) is a connecting alif (hamzat al-waṣl) carrying a kasra, added as a vocalic prop because the imperative stem begins with a consonant cluster that could not otherwise be pronounced — nothing is dropped; this helping vowel is prefixed.
20.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, to beat; also figuratively to set forth (an example) or to travel

21.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
21.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

22.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
22.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

23.meaning: Fingertips or finger-joints; the ends of the fingers and toes. By extension it can stand for the fingers or extremities themselves.
23.grammar: An indefinite noun. The final -in (written with tanwīn, a doubled vowel-sign) marks it as both indefinite ('fingertips', not 'the fingertips') and grammatically genitive — the case that typically follows a preposition or links one noun to another. It is a collective noun referring to the fingertips as a group.
23.root: ب-ن-ن (b-n-n) — relating to the fingertips / finger-ends

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
2.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

3.meaning: They opposed, resisted, or split off into hostile contention against someone — to set oneself in conflict with another, taking the opposing 'side' (shiqq).
3.grammar: A past-tense verb of the mutual/reciprocal pattern (form III), which adds the sense of acting against or toward another party — here 'to be in opposition with'. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (a masculine plural group) and the action is completed (past).
3.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave; figuratively to break away into opposition, to be at odds

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
5.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

6.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
6.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
6.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: He opposes, breaks away from, sets himself in contention against, or splits from. The verb conveys hostile opposition and rupture, as if standing on the opposite side.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb of the mutual/confrontational pattern ('to set oneself against'). The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The base would end in a silent (jussive) consonant, but because of the doubled root letters a helping vowel -i is added; the jussive is the mood used in conditional clauses ('whoever opposes…').
7.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave; hence to be at odds, oppose

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
9.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a messenger

10.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
10.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty — describing something powerful and unsparing in its degree.
12.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('severe, intense'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or predicate.
12.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

13.meaning: The punishment, penalty, or retribution; a consequence imposed in requital for wrongdoing.
13.grammar: A definite noun with prefixed al- ("the"). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… of …") or follows a preposition.
13.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow/come after; consequence, punishment

1.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

2.meaning: A command meaning 'so taste it!' — to experience or undergo something directly, here applied to it (a thing or punishment). 'Tasting' is often used figuratively for experiencing a consequence firsthand.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb with the fa- prefix marking result or sequence ('so', 'then'). The -ū ending is the plural masculine command marker ('you all'). The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'it/him', the thing being tasted. Together: 'so taste it, all of you'.
2.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste; figuratively to experience or undergo

3.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
3.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

4.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
4.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

5.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
5.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

5.meaning: You (a group) met, encountered, or came face to face with someone — often used of meeting an opponent in confrontation.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -tum ending marks the subject as 'you' (a masculine plural group) and the action as completed. The final short -u is a helping vowel added so the word can join smoothly to whatever follows (it eases pronunciation before another word beginning with a connecting alif).
5.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

8.meaning: Advancing in a mass, marching forward in a crowd that creeps along the ground by sheer numbers; a slow, heavy military advance of a throng.

parts.en: a marching advance / throng creeping forward

8.grammar: A noun used to describe the manner of an action. The -an ending (written with tanwīn, a doubled vowel-sign) is the indefinite accusative; in this kind of usage it typically explains the circumstance or manner of something — i.e. 'advancing / in a marching throng'. The root sense is of a body so large it seems to crawl forward.
8.root: ز-ح-ف (z-ḥ-f) — to crawl, creep, advance slowly in a mass

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
9.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

10.meaning: You (a group) turn toward them — to give a side or direction to someone, here in the sense of presenting (something) to them or wheeling round to face them.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive pattern (form II) meaning to turn or direct a side toward. The t- prefix with the -ū ending marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural). The attached -hum is the object 'them'. The final short -u is a helping vowel easing the join to a following word. (In commands or after certain particles this verb can shift to mean 'turn your backs' / flee.)
10.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to turn toward or away; to take charge, be an ally

11.meaning: The backs — the plural of 'back', the rear of the body. Turning one's 'backs' is a common image for fleeing or retreating.
11.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the backs'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The form adbār is a broken (irregular internal) plural of the singular dubur, 'back / hindpart'.
11.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back, rear, hind part; that which comes behind

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: He turns or directs (a side) toward them — to wheel something around to face them, or to turn his own back to them. From the same root that yields the ideas of nearness, alliance, and turning.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive pattern (form II) meaning to turn or direct a side toward. The yu- prefix marks a single masculine 'he' as subject. The verb is in the jussive (clipped) mood — the final consonant carries no long vowel — a form used after conditional or certain particles. The attached -him means 'to them'.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to turn toward or away; to take charge, be an ally

3.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
3.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

4.meaning: His back — the rear of his body. Turning one's back is a stock image for fleeing from battle.
4.grammar: A noun with a possessive ending. The -a vowel before the pronoun is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object (the thing acted upon). The attached -hu means 'his', so the whole is 'his back'.
4.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back, rear, hind part; that which comes behind

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: One who turns aside or swerves — wheeling away to one side as a maneuver rather than in flight, e.g. shifting position to regroup or gain advantage.
6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) of the reflexive intensive pattern (form V), describing someone in the act of turning himself to one edge or side. The -an ending (tanwīn, a doubled vowel-sign) is the indefinite accusative, the case that here typically describes the state or manner in which someone acts — 'as one swerving aside'.
6.root: ح-ر-ف (ḥ-r-f) — edge, border, brink; to turn or deviate to a side

7.meaning: For (the purpose of) fighting; belonging to battle or combat. Qitāl is sustained mutual fighting or warfare.
7.grammar: A verbal noun ('fighting') of the mutual pattern (form III), naming combat as an act done between two parties. The li- prefix means 'for' or 'belonging to' and always puts the following noun into the genitive case, shown here by the -in ending (tanwīn, a doubled vowel-sign), which also marks it indefinite ('a fight / battle').
7.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay; in this pattern, to fight one another

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: One who withdraws to join or take up a position with a group — moving to attach oneself to a body of people, securing a place or 'side' alongside them.

parts.en: one withdrawing to join / take position

9.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) of the reflexive intensive pattern (form V), describing someone in the act of taking up a position or aligning himself with a group. The -an ending (tanwīn, a doubled vowel-sign) is the indefinite accusative, the case that here typically describes the state or manner in which someone acts — 'as one joining / repositioning'.
9.root: ح-و-ز (ḥ-w-z) — to gather, take possession of, take up a space or side

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
10.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

11.meaning: A group, band, or company of people — a detachment or faction, especially a body of fighters. It denotes a portion of a larger whole that has banded together.
11.grammar: A feminine singular noun, here indefinite (no 'the'). The ending '-in' (the tā' marbūṭa pronounced with nunation, '-tin') is the indefinite genitive: it marks the noun as 'a group' linked to/governed by a preceding word, such as a counting particle or preposition.
11.root: ف-أ-ي (f-ʾ-y) — to split off; a faction/group

12.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
12.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

13.meaning: Means 'he returned / came back (bearing something)' — to come back drawing a burden upon oneself; with an unwelcome thing it conveys incurring or bringing it back on oneself.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb with a built-in doer 'he' (a single male): 'he returned / came back laden.' The past tense presents it as completed. It is commonly paired with 'with' (bi-) to mean returning carrying or having earned something.
13.root: ب-و-ء (b-w-ʾ) — to return, come back, settle into / incur

14.meaning: 'With anger / wrath' — the preposition bi- ('with') joined to an indefinite noun for intense displeasure and indignation.
14.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with', and it always puts its noun in the genitive. The -in ending (tanwīn) marks the noun as indefinite ('some/a measure of wrath') and genitive, the case required after a preposition.

15.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
15.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: Means 'and his refuge / abode' — the place to which one ultimately resorts and where one comes to rest or dwell.
17.grammar: A place-noun (a 'place of …' form) meaning 'place of resort / dwelling.' The attached -hu is the possessive 'his / its.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' The -u vowel on the attached pronoun (hu) reflects its base form after a long vowel.
17.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, resort to, give refuge

18.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
18.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

19.meaning: And how evil / wretched (it is)! — wa joined to biʾsa, a fixed verb of blame used to condemn something as bad, the opposite of niʿma ('how excellent'). It expresses strong disapproval.
19.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus biʾsa, a frozen verb of blame ('how wretched is …') that does not change for tense. It introduces strong condemnation of whatever follows as its subject, the counterpart of niʿma ('how good is …').

20.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
20.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
20.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: A two-part device meaning 'did not …' — it combines 'and/then so' with a negating word that turns a present-tense verb into a flat statement that something did NOT happen in the past.
1.grammar: A connecting particle fa- ('and so / then') joined to the negative particle lam. Lam negates the past: it precedes a present-tense verb but flips its meaning to 'did not do', and it puts that following verb into the jussive (clipped) form.

2.meaning: You (a group) kill or slay them — to put them to death.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural). The verb appears in a clipped (jussive/subjunctive) form — the ending has lost its final n — as happens after certain particles. The attached -hum is the object 'them': 'you (all) kill them'.
2.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

3.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
3.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: He killed them — a single male agent put them to death. The verb can also be ascribed to Allah, meaning that the true slaying was His doing.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare stem with the final -a marks a single masculine 'he' as subject and the action as completed. The attached -hum is the object 'them', so the whole means 'he killed them'.
5.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
6.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

7.meaning: You (one person) threw, cast, or hurled (something). Can apply to flinging an object such as dust, an arrow, or a stone.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ta ending marks the subject as 'you' (a single male) and the action as completed: 'you threw'. The root's final weak letter (y) surfaces in this form as -ay- before the ending.
7.root: ر-م-ي (r-m-y) — to throw, cast, hurl, shoot

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

9.meaning: You (one person) threw, cast, or hurled (something). Can apply to flinging an object such as dust, an arrow, or a stone.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ta ending marks the subject as 'you' (a single male) and the action as completed: 'you threw'. The root's final weak letter (y) surfaces in this form as -ay- before the ending.
9.root: ر-م-ي (r-m-y) — to throw, cast, hurl, shoot

10.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
10.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.
10.root: — (particle)

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: He threw, cast, or hurled (something) — said of a single male agent; may also be ascribed to Allah, meaning the true casting was His.

parts.en: he (past tense, 3rd person) with weak final letter

12.grammar: A past-tense verb for a single masculine 'he', with the action completed. Because the root ends in a weak letter (y), the third-person ending appears as a long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra, ى) rather than the usual short vowel: 'he threw'.
12.root: ر-م-ي (r-m-y) — to throw, cast, hurl, shoot

13.meaning: And so that He may test, prove, or try — to put someone through a trial in order to bring out and make evident what they are. The prefixed particle expresses purpose: 'and in order that He may…'.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of the causative pattern (form IV), 'to put to the test'. The yu- prefix marks 'he' as subject. The li- particle ('so that') expresses purpose and puts the verb into the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending — the mood used for an intended result ('in order that He may test'). The leading wa- means 'and'.
13.root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w) — to test, try, put to the proof

14.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
14.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

15.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
15.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
15.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

16.meaning: A testing or trial — an ordeal or affliction sent to prove someone. The same word can also denote a favor or blessing that tests one's gratitude; its core idea is being put to the proof, whether through hardship or good.
16.grammar: A verbal noun ('a testing / trial'). The -an ending (tanwīn, a doubled vowel-sign written here over a final hamza) marks it as both indefinite ('a trial') and accusative — the case that often marks the object of a verb or specifies the thing or purpose involved.
16.root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w) — to test, try, put to the proof

17.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
17.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.
17.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

18.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
18.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
20.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

21.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

2.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
2.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: One who weakens or saps the strength of something — the doer of an act that renders another feeble or frustrates its force.
4.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) of the causative pattern (form IV), 'one who makes weak'. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject or the one doing the action. Such a participle often governs a following noun in the genitive, giving the sense 'weakener OF …'.
4.root: و-ه-ن (w-h-n) — to be weak, feeble, frail

5.meaning: Scheme, plot, or cunning stratagem — a carefully devised plan, often with the sense of secret contrivance against another.
5.grammar: A verbal noun ('plotting / a scheme'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …', e.g. the scheme OF someone) or follows a preposition or oath particle.
5.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to scheme, plot, contrive a stratagem

6.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
6.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: You (a group) seek a decisive opening or victory — to ask for a judgment to be rendered between two parties, or for triumph to be granted. The root joins the ideas of 'opening', 'deciding', and 'conquest'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb of the 'seeking' pattern (form X), which adds the sense of asking or seeking for oneself — here 'to seek a decisive opening / victory'. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural): 'you (all) seek victory'.
2.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; to decide/judge between, to grant victory or conquest

3.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
3.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

4.meaning: 'he/it came to you' — the arrival of someone or something to a group of people addressed.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb ('came'), done by 'he/it'. The verb is intransitive, so the attached -kum ('you,' plural) is not a direct object but a recipient/directional pronoun marking the people the arrival is toward ('came to you'); it is voweled -kumu before a following word. So: 'he/it came to you (all).'

5.meaning: The opening, the deciding victory, the breaking-through. From a root meaning 'to open,' it denotes a decisive resolution between opposing parties — a triumph or judgment that 'opens' what was closed and settles a dispute. It can also mean an arbitration or a granting of relief.
5.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The al- prefix means 'the.' The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('it is the …').

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
6.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

7.meaning: You (plural) cease, stop, desist, leave off. From a root meaning 'to reach the end / come to a limit,' the verb conveys bringing an action to its terminating point — refraining from and abandoning what one was doing.
7.grammar: A present-tense Form VIII (iftaʿala) verb. The ta- prefix marks 'you'; the characteristic Form VIII infix -t- sits after the first root letter n, while the weak final root letter (y) is dropped in conjugation, leaving the stem -ntahi-. The -ū ending marks a plural masculine 'you all,' and the dropped final nūn (-ū rather than -ūna) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after certain particles such as 'if,' 'so that,' or in conditions.
7.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to reach a limit, to forbid, to cease

8.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
8.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

9.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
9.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
9.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

10.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
10.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

11.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
11.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

12.meaning: You (plural) return, go back, revert, do something again. From a root meaning 'to return / repeat,' it denotes coming back to a prior state or resuming a previous course of action.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks a plural masculine 'you all.' The missing final nūn (-ū not -ūna) signals the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after conditional or purpose particles ('if you return …').
12.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, to repeat, to come back

13.meaning: We return, We go back, We do (it) again. From a root meaning 'to return / repeat,' it expresses the speakers reverting to or resuming a prior action.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means 'we.' The vowelless final consonant (sukūn on the d, giving naʿud rather than naʿūdu) marks the jussive mood — the clipped form used in the answer to a condition ('… then We will return') or after a jussive particle.
13.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, to repeat, to come back

14.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
14.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

15.meaning: To avail / to be of use / to ward off need; from a verb meaning to enrich or make independent, hence 'to be of any benefit' or 'to suffice (someone) against' a threat — typically used to deny that something can help at all.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a on the stem-vowel (-iya). The tu- prefix marks the doer as 'it/she' (third-person feminine singular) or a second-person 'you'. The subjunctive typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or 'will not', expressing a non-factual, hoped-for, or negated action rather than a plain statement.
15.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient; hence to avail/suffice

16.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
16.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

17.meaning: Your (plural) band, group, or company — especially a body of fighters or a contingent. A fiʾa is a faction or troop that one falls back upon for support. The attached pronoun makes it 'your group.'
17.grammar: A feminine noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u before the suffix is the nominative ending, generally marking the word as the subject of a clause ('your band …'). The suffix -kum means 'your,' addressing a group.
17.root: ف-أ-ي / ف-ي-أ (f-ʾ-y) — a group that one resorts to, a faction

18.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
18.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

19.meaning: 'And even if / and though' — a particle pairing 'and' with 'law', which introduces a hypothetical or concessive condition ('even supposing that …').
19.grammar: A compound particle: 'and' + the conditional 'law'. 'Law' introduces a supposition, often a counter-to-expectation one ('even if …'), and is typically followed by a past-tense verb that carries a hypothetical sense. It is a function word with no case ending.

20.meaning: It (feminine) became many / numerous / abundant. A past-tense verb from a root meaning 'to be much or many,' expressing that something grew great in number or quantity.
20.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine singular subject — 'she/it did,' used here for a grammatically feminine noun. The perfect tense presents the action as completed or established.
20.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

21.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
21.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
23.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

24.meaning: The believers — those who have faith. The active participle of a Form IV verb meaning 'to believe, to have faith, to grant security.' A muʾmin is one who affirms and trusts, and who thereby finds and gives security; the plural denotes the community of the faithful.
24.grammar: A definite masculine plural noun (active participle). The al- means 'the.' The plural ending -īna marks 'the believers' in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case — the form used when the word is a direct object or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Obey! — a plural command to comply, submit, and do as one is told. The verb denotes willing, active obedience and yielding to authority.
4.grammar: A Form IV imperative (command) built on the root for obedience. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee — 'obey, all of you!'. (The written final alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.)

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
6.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a messenger

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: 'They turned away / they turned their backs / they turned aside'. It conveys turning oneself away from something, often implying rejection or withdrawal.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural: the ending '-aw' means 'they (did) …'. The Form V pattern (with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle letter) gives a reflexive sense — turning oneself away. It states a completed act.
8.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near/turn toward; in this form, to turn away

9.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
9.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

10.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
10.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

11.meaning: You (plural) hear, listen, give ear. A present-tense verb from a root meaning 'to hear,' denoting the act of perceiving by ear, and by extension heeding or paying attention.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine 'you all.' The full ending -ūna (with the final nūn intact) is the indicative mood, the default form used for plain factual statements ('you (all) hear').
11.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, to listen, to heed

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
2.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: Like those who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, meaning 'similar to the ones who…' and pointing to a group defined by what follows.
3.grammar: A compound of the preposition ka- ('like, as'), expressing resemblance, and the masculine plural relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). The relative pronoun is fixed in form and introduces a description; it does not change for case.

4.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

6.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
6.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: They hear / listen to — to perceive by hearing, and often to give heed to what is heard.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the third-person masculine plural ('they'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual action.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: Worst, most evil, gravest in harm; or as a noun, evil/harm itself. From a root denoting wickedness and badness. In this comparative/superlative form it means 'more/most evil' or 'the worst of.'
2.grammar: A noun used in the superlative/comparative sense. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks a direct object, or appears when the word is the first term of a possessive 'X of Y' construct ('the worst of …').
2.root: ش-ر-ر (sh-r-r) — evil, wickedness, harm

3.meaning: The moving creatures, the beasts, all that crawls or treads the earth. From a root meaning 'to move / creep along,' a dābba is any living, moving animal; the plural covers the whole range of earthly creatures.
3.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun. The al- means 'the' (its l assimilates into the following d, written dd). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('the … of the creatures') or follows a preposition.
3.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move, creep, tread along

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: The deaf — those who cannot hear. From a root meaning 'to be deaf / blocked up,' this is the plural of aṣamm, denoting the loss of hearing, often used figuratively for unwillingness to heed.
6.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun. The al- means 'the' (its l assimilates into the following ṣ). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject or predicate of a sentence ('they are the deaf').
6.root: ص-م-م (ṣ-m-m) — to be deaf, blocked, solid

7.meaning: The dumb / mute — those who cannot speak. From a root meaning 'to be unable to speak,' this is the plural of abkam, often used figuratively for those who will not voice the truth.
7.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun. The al- means 'the.' The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject or predicate of a sentence ('they are the mute').

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: 'They understand / use reason.' To comprehend, reason, and grasp things with the intellect — to 'tie down' meaning with the mind, to think rationally and exercise sound judgment.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they [do]' for a group of males or a mixed group. The full -ūna ending (with the final -na intact) marks the indicative mood, i.e. a plain factual statement. The root sense is binding/restraining, hence using the mind to 'hold' meaning.
10.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to bind, restrain; intellect, reason

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: 'He knew / came to know / had knowledge of'. The verb denotes knowing with certainty — being aware of and acquainted with a thing's reality.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a completed action done by 'he'. It states that the knowing took place and is settled.
2.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, awareness

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
4.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

5.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
5.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

6.meaning: He would surely have made them hear / caused them to hear. From the root 'to hear' in its causative (Form IV) sense — 'to make someone hear' — with an emphatic particle prefixed and an attached object 'them.'
6.grammar: A past-tense causative (Form IV) verb. The prefixed la- is an emphatic 'surely / indeed,' frequently the answer to a hypothetical 'if.' The verb's a-…-a shape means 'he caused to hear.' The final -a before the suffix is the standard past third-person masculine vowel, and -hum is the object 'them.'
6.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear; (Form IV) to make hear

7.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
7.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

8.meaning: He made them hear / caused them to hear. The causative (Form IV) of the root 'to hear' — 'to make someone hear' — with the attached object 'them.'
8.grammar: A past-tense causative (Form IV) verb. The a-…-a pattern carries the meaning 'he caused to hear.' The -a before the suffix is the third-person masculine singular past ending ('he did'), and -hum is the attached object pronoun 'them.'
8.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear; (Form IV) to make hear

9.meaning: They surely turned away / would have turned away. From a Form V verb meaning 'to turn oneself away, to turn one's back, to take charge or take as an ally,' here in the sense of turning aside or away, with an emphatic particle prefixed.
9.grammar: A past-tense reflexive (Form V) verb. The prefixed la- is emphatic 'surely,' often answering a hypothetical 'if.' The ending -aw is the third-person masculine plural past ('they did'), for a verb whose root ends in a weak letter. Form V (ta- + doubled middle) gives the sense of doing something to/for oneself — here 'turning oneself away.'
9.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, allegiance, taking charge, turning toward/away

10.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
10.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.
10.root: — (conjunction plus pronoun; no root)

11.meaning: Ones who turn away, who avert themselves and refuse — people who deliberately turn their faces and backs away, declining and shunning what is presented to them.
11.grammar: An active participle (a doer-noun: 'ones who turn away') from a verb meaning 'to turn aside / avert oneself'. The 'mu-' prefix marks the doer of this verb-pattern. The -ūna ending marks the masculine-plural nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence or what something is being described as.
11.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to be wide, present sideways; (this pattern) to turn away, avert oneself

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Respond! Answer! Comply! A plural command from a Form X verb meaning 'to answer a call, to respond favorably, to grant a request.' It calls on a group to give a positive, obedient response.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb, Form X, addressed to a plural 'you all.' It begins with the connecting (helping) alif pronounced when starting speech. The -ū ending directs the order to a group of males (or mixed group): 'all of you, respond!'

5.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
5.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

6.meaning: And to the Messenger — the one sent (with a message). Rasūl is one dispatched bearing a communication, i.e. a messenger or envoy; with the article it denotes 'the Messenger.' The word here carries a connecting 'and,' a preposition 'to/for,' and 'the.'
6.grammar: A definite masculine noun preceded by particles. wa- is 'and,' li- is the preposition 'to/for,' and l- is 'the' (its l assimilates into the following r). The final -i is the genitive ending, required here because the noun follows the preposition 'to/for.'
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

7.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

8.meaning: He called you (plural), summoned you, invited you. From a root meaning 'to call / summon / invite / pray,' the verb denotes calling out to someone, with the attached object 'you all.'
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The base daʿā is third-person masculine singular past ('he called'), its final weak letter appearing as a long ā. The suffix -kum is the object 'you all,' addressing a group.
8.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, supplicate

9.meaning: 'Regarding what / as to that which'. A compound joining the preposition 'to/for/regarding' with the relative pronoun 'what / that which', introducing a clause about a thing or matter.
9.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'to', 'for', or 'regarding'. 'mā' is a relative pronoun meaning 'what' or 'that which', used for things and ideas (not persons). It has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

10.meaning: 'He gives life' or 'He brings to life' — a causative verb from the root meaning life: to make alive, to revive, to grant living existence to what was lifeless.
10.grammar: Present/future tense. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in the causative (form IV) pattern; the imperfect without a jussive/subjunctive ending expresses ongoing or future action ('he gives / will give life'). The attached -kum is a plural object pronoun, 'you (all)'.
10.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, living

11.meaning: And know! — the connector 'and' joined to a command to know, realize, or be aware of something. A direct summons to a group to take firm notice.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a group. The ending -ū marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all, know!'). Prefixed with wa- ('and').

12.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
12.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
13.root: — (proper name)

14.meaning: He / it comes between, intervenes, stands as a barrier, separates. From a root meaning 'to turn / interpose / change,' the verb denotes coming between two things so as to bar or divide them.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it does'). The final -u is the indicative ending, the default form used for plain factual statements ('he comes between').
14.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — to turn, interpose, come between, change

15.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
15.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
15.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

16.meaning: The man; the person, the human individual (the noun for a man as a single human being).
