16.grammar: A definite masculine noun in the genitive case, shown by the final -i, which typically appears after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of the man').

17.meaning: And his heart — the seat of understanding, feeling, intention, and faith. Qalb denotes the inner core of a person (commonly 'heart' or 'mind'), the locus of thought and emotion. The word carries a connecting 'and' and the possessive 'his.'
17.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun, preceded by 'and.' wa- means 'and.' The -i ending is genitive — the case that links the noun to a preceding noun or follows a preposition; the -hi form of 'his' is the variant used after an i-vowel.
17.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn, to overturn

18.meaning: And that … — a connecting 'and' plus the emphatic particle anna ('that / indeed') with the attached pronoun 'he/it.' anna introduces and stresses a statement, like saying 'and (the fact) that he/it is …'
18.grammar: A particle combination. wa- is 'and.' anna is an emphatic conjunction meaning 'that' (it introduces a noun-clause and gives it the force of 'indeed'). The attached -hu is its subject pronoun, 'he/it.' anna requires the following noun to be in the accusative case.

19.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
19.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

20.meaning: 'You all will be gathered / assembled / mustered' — to be brought together into one place, as a crowd is rounded up. The root is strongly associated with the gathering of all people for the Day of Resurrection.
20.grammar: A present/future-tense passive verb ('to be gathered'). The tu-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all') as the ones acted upon, with the action ongoing or yet to come. The retained final -na indicates the verb is in its base (indicative) state.

1.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
1.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

2.meaning: A trial, test, temptation, affliction, or sedition. Fitna is a weighty term: originally the smelting of metal to test its purity, it comes to mean any testing or tribulation — persecution, civil strife, seductive enticement, or a probing ordeal that reveals what is within.
2.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun. The ending -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a trial') and in the accusative case — typically the case of a direct object or of a noun functioning as the predicate after certain verbs.
2.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire, to try, to tempt, to afflict

3.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
3.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

4.meaning: It will surely strike / befall / afflict. From a root meaning 'to hit the mark, to reach, to befall,' the verb denotes a calamity or event reaching and touching someone, intensified here so it reads 'it shall certainly afflict.'
4.grammar: A present-tense causative (Form IV) verb carrying the emphatic ending -anna (the 'heavy' nūn of emphasis), which adds the force of 'certainly / surely shall.' The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she will'), agreeing with a grammatically feminine noun.
4.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, to be right, to befall

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
6.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

7.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
7.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
7.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

8.meaning: Specifically, exclusively, in particular; a special class or select group. From a root meaning 'to be particular / set apart,' khāṣṣa denotes something singled out — affecting only a special few rather than all in general.
8.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun, commonly used adverbially. The ending -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case; in the accusative such a word often works as an adverb of manner or state, meaning 'specifically / particularly.'
8.root: خ-ص-ص (kh-ṣ-ṣ) — to single out, to be particular, to set apart

9.meaning: And know! — the connector 'and' joined to a command to know, realize, or be aware of something. A direct summons to a group to take firm notice.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a group. The ending -ū marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all, know!'). Prefixed with wa- ('and').
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

10.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
10.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: Severe, intense, harsh, or mighty — describing something powerful and unsparing in its degree.
12.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('severe, intense'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or predicate.
12.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

13.meaning: The punishment, penalty, or retribution; a consequence imposed in requital for wrongdoing.
13.grammar: A definite noun with prefixed al- ("the"). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… of …") or follows a preposition.
13.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow/come after; consequence, punishment

1.meaning: A command to a group meaning 'and remember / and call to mind / and mention.' The root spans both calling something to memory and uttering it aloud.
1.grammar: The connector 'wa' (and) plus a command (imperative) verb 'remember/mention.' The ending -ū addresses a masculine plural group ('you all remember!').
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

3.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
3.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

4.meaning: 'Few', 'little', 'a small amount/number'. Describes something scant in quantity — a small group of people or a small portion of a thing.
4.grammar: A descriptive adjective (or noun). The '-un' ending is the nominative case with nunation ('tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a few', not 'the few'); the nominative typically marks the subject or a predicate.

5.meaning: Those who are treated as weak, oppressed, and considered of no account — people whom others reckon defenseless and overpower or push around. It conveys being on the receiving end of contempt and domination, not merely physical weakness.

parts.en: one who is made/deemed (passive participle prefix, form X)

5.grammar: A passive participle of the seeking/reckoning pattern (form X), masculine plural. The mus-ta- prefix here carries the sense 'reckoned to be / treated as,' so the word means people deemed weak by others. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the subject/naming case ('those who are...'); it would shift to -īna when the word is an object or follows a preposition.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

8.meaning: You fear, dread, or apprehend — to be afraid of something or to anticipate a feared outcome.
8.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks a plural subject in the indicative mood, typically describing an ongoing or general action ('you (all) fear').

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
9.root: — (particle; no root)

10.meaning: He snatches you away suddenly — to seize and carry off swiftly by surprise, the way a bird of prey swoops and grabs. It pictures an abrupt, forcible abduction.

parts.en: snatch/seize away (form V stem: ta- + doubled middle root)

10.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he snatches'), on form V (tafaʿʿala). Form V is built by adding the ta- element to form II; the doubling of the middle root letter (-khaṭṭ-) belongs to form II, and form V layers the ta- on top of it, giving a reflexive/intensive sense of a sudden, sweeping seizure. The ya- prefix signals 'he,' and the mood vowel -u (carried just before the pronoun: ...ṭṭaf-u-) is the indicative, the form for a plain statement; it would become -a (subjunctive) after a particle such as 'that' or 'lest,' or drop to a bare consonant (jussive) in conditions and prohibitions. The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you (plural)'; its vowel is lengthened to -kumu for ease of pronunciation before a following word.
10.root: خ-ط-ف (kh-ṭ-f) — snatching, swift seizing, carrying off

11.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
11.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
11.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

12.meaning: Then He gave you shelter and refuge — to take someone in, provide a safe place of return and lodging. The 'fa-' adds the sense 'and so / thereupon.'
12.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('He sheltered'). The opening fa- is a connector meaning 'then / and so.' The final -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you (plural).' The long final ā belongs to a weak-ending verb whose third root letter is a vowel-like consonant.
12.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — taking refuge, giving shelter, a place of return

13.meaning: And He reinforced you, backed you up, gave you support and strength — to aid by adding power, to fortify and bolster.

parts.en: he strengthened, supported, reinforced (intensive form II)

13.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('He strengthened'), on the intensive doubled pattern (form II) conveying thorough reinforcement. The opening wa- means 'and.' The final -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you (plural).'
13.root: أ-ي-د (ʾ-y-d) — strength, support, backing

14.meaning: 'with His help / aid / victory' — the noun for divinely granted help or victory, governed by 'with/by' and joined to the pronoun 'His.'
14.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by means of') + the verbal noun naṣr ('help, support, victory') + the possessive pronoun -hi ('his/its'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending required after the preposition bi-. Naṣr denotes the granting of aid that brings triumph; when the pronoun refers to Allah it means 'with Allah's help.'

15.meaning: And He provided for you, granted you sustenance — to bestow the provision (food, livelihood, and every good) that a creature needs and lives on.
15.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('He provided'). The opening wa- means 'and.' The final -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you (plural).' The -a- vowels are the standard pattern of a plain past-tense verb.
15.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, livelihood granted by Allah

16.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
16.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

17.meaning: 'The good/wholesome things' — that which is pure, pleasant, and lawful, especially good and agreeable food.
17.grammar: A descriptive noun ('good, wholesome') made definite by al- ('the') and put in the feminine sound plural. The -āti ending is the feminine plural in the object or genitive state (its counterpart -ātu is the subject form). It names things characterized as pure and good.
17.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pure, wholesome, pleasant

18.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

18.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

19.meaning: 'You (all) give thanks / are grateful'. To recognize a kindness and acknowledge it — with the heart, tongue, and deeds — toward the one who bestowed it.
19.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine 'you' in the ongoing (indicative) mood — 'you all give thanks'. The retained '-na' shows the verb stands free of any negating or governing particle.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: You betray, act treacherously, break a trust — to be unfaithful to what was entrusted or to a covenant, the opposite of being trustworthy.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all...'). The ta- prefix signals 'you,' and the -ū ending marks the plural 'you.' The dropping of the usual final -na (so -ū rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in a dependent mood, the form used after particles meaning 'that,' 'so as to,' or in negative commands. The hollow root's middle vowel surfaces as a long ū.
5.root: خ-و-ن (kh-w-n) — betrayal, treachery, breaking a trust

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
6.root: — (proper name)

7.meaning: A compound: 'and the Messenger'. It joins 'and', the definite article 'the', and the noun rasūl — one who is sent, an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver a message.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates in sound to the following 'r', hence r-rasūl). The noun is on the faʿūl pattern meaning 'one sent'. The final -a ending marks the accusative case — commonly the direct object of a verb ('… the Messenger' as the one being acted upon).
7.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a message or envoy

8.meaning: And/or you betray, act treacherously, break a trust — the same verb of unfaithfulness to what is entrusted, joined by 'and.'
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and/or') joined to a present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all...'). The ta- prefix signals 'you,' and the -ū ending marks the plural. The absence of the final -na shows a dependent mood (after 'that/so as to' or a negation). The hollow root's middle vowel appears as a long ū.
8.root: خ-و-ن (kh-w-n) — betrayal, treachery, breaking a trust

9.meaning: Your trusts — the things committed to your safekeeping: deposits, responsibilities, and obligations one is duty-bound to honor and return intact.
9.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('trusts') with the attached possessive 'your (plural)' = -kum. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/linking) case, here showing ownership: 'trusts OF you' = 'your trusts.' This case also appears after prepositions and oath particles.
9.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust, security, being faithful

10.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
10.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

11.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
11.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: And know! — the connector 'and' joined to a command to know, realize, or be aware of something. A direct summons to a group to take firm notice.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a group. The ending -ū marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all, know!'). Prefixed with wa- ('and').

2.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
2.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.
2.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Your wealth, your possessions and property — the goods and money one owns. Singular sense is 'māl' (wealth); this is its plural, 'riches/assets.'
3.grammar: A plural noun ('wealth, possessions') with the attached possessive 'your (plural)' = -kum. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, the form a noun takes when it is the doer or topic of a sentence ('your wealth [is/does...]').

4.meaning: And your children, your offspring — one's sons and daughters; the plural of 'walad' (a child/son).
4.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a plural noun ('children') with the attached possessive 'your (plural)' = -kum. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, used when the noun is the doer or topic of a sentence.

5.meaning: A trial, test, or temptation; affliction or seduction that puts faith and character to the proof and may lead one into discord or sin.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the -ah/-at ending) in the nominative case. The -un ending pairs the nominative marker -u (subject / predicate form) with nunation (-n), marking it indefinite: 'a trial'.
5.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire, try; trial, temptation

6.meaning: 'And that …' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle anna, which introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting a fact emphatically (roughly 'and indeed that …'), and grammatically governs the noun that follows it.
6.grammar: A conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to anna, an emphatic particle meaning 'that' (asserting a fact). Anna puts the following noun into the accusative case and typically links a clause to a preceding verb of saying, knowing, or perceiving.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: 'With him / in his keeping / that he has' — combining the locational word 'ind ('at, with, in the presence/possession of') with the pronoun 'him'. It conveys that something is held by, present with, or belongs to him.
8.grammar: 'ʿinda' is an adverb of place/possession that always governs a following word in the genitive; here it takes the attached pronoun -hu ('him/his'). The -a on 'ʿinda' is its fixed accusative-style ending as an adverbial. The pronoun -hu means the thing is located with, or owned by, a single male.

9.meaning: Means 'a reward, a wage, a recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or deeds — payment earned, compensation, or a reward.
9.grammar: A noun in the nominative, indefinite ('a reward'). The -un ending (a doubled-vowel tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a/some') and the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a thing being asserted to exist ('there is a reward').
9.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense

10.meaning: Great, immense, mighty, or tremendous — describing something vast in scale, weight, or significance.
10.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('great, mighty'). The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative; an adjective in this form typically agrees with and describes an indefinite nominative noun.
10.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: You guard yourselves, you are wary and conscious of Allah — to shield yourself by being mindful and reverently cautious, avoiding what brings harm or displeasure.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in form VIII (the reflexive 'iftaʿala,' here 'to protect oneself / be God-conscious'), from a weak root so its final letter has dropped away. The 'ta-' prefix plus the '-ū' ending mark a second-person masculine plural 'you (all).' The loss of the final '-na' shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after certain particles (such as those meaning 'that,' 'not,' or in conditions).

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
6.root: — (proper name)

7.meaning: He makes, appoints, grants, or brings about — a very general verb of causing something to be or assigning something to someone; here in a form used after conditions ('He will make/grant').
7.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he makes/grants'). The ya- prefix signals 'he.' The bare consonant ending (sukūn, no final vowel: -jʿal rather than -jʿalu) is the jussive mood, the clipped form used in conditional 'if... then...' clauses and certain commands and negations.

8.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
8.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

9.meaning: A criterion — that which separates and distinguishes truth from falsehood, right from wrong; a means of decisive discernment or a deliverance that sets things apart. From the sense of 'parting/separating.'

parts.en: criterion, distinguisher between truth and falsehood

9.grammar: A masculine noun built on a pattern of broad verbal meaning ('the act/means of distinguishing'). The final -an is the indefinite object ending ('a criterion'), marking the noun as indefinite and in the object/accusative case — the form taken when the noun is what a verb acts upon.
9.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — separating, distinguishing, dividing truth from falsehood

10.meaning: And He blots out, covers over, and expiates — to wipe away wrongdoings so they are concealed and pardoned. The root sense is 'to cover'; in this form it means to cancel out sins.

parts.en: blot out, expiate, cover over (intensive form II)

10.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he blots out'), on the intensive doubled pattern (form II) with its yu- prefix. The bare consonant ending (sukūn, no final vowel: -kaffir not -kaffiru) is the jussive mood, used in conditional clauses and after certain particles.
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — covering over; (form II) wiping away/expiating sins

11.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
11.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

12.meaning: Your evil deeds, misdeeds, or bad actions — the plural of a word denoting a wrong or offense, something that brings harm or ill, paired with the second-person plural 'your.'
12.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun ('evil deeds') with the attached pronoun -kum ('your,' for a group). The -āt ending is the regular feminine plural. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which here signals possession — the noun is joined to a following possessor ('the misdeeds OF you' = 'your misdeeds').
12.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to harm

13.meaning: A compound: 'and He will forgive' / 'and may He forgive'. It joins 'and' to an imperfect verb meaning to forgive, pardon, and cover over sins — to wipe away guilt and shield the wrongdoer from its consequences.
13.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb stands in the jussive mood — shown by its clipped, vowel-less ending — typically appearing after certain particles or as the result-clause of a condition ('… he will forgive / that he may forgive').
13.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield, and pardon; forgiveness

14.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

15.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
15.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
15.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

16.meaning: Owner of / possessor of / endowed with — a word that does not stand alone but means 'the one who has' whatever noun follows it, ascribing that quality or possession to someone.

parts.en: possessor of, owner of, endowed with

16.grammar: A possessive noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', always followed by another noun in the genitive. The final -ū form here is the nominative case, used when this word names the subject or is the thing being described; it inherently requires a following noun to complete its sense ('owner OF …').
16.root: — (no triliteral root; an irregular noun of possession)

17.meaning: Bounty, grace, abundant favour — generous giving beyond what is owed or merely sufficient; overflowing goodness and surplus.
17.grammar: A definite noun ('the bounty'). The al- prefix means 'the'; the final -i is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by a preceding word (the '… OF …' relationship).
17.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to exceed, be left over; abundance, surplus, favour

18.meaning: Great, immense, magnificent — vast in importance, weight, and grandeur; awe-inspiring in scale.
18.grammar: A definite adjective ('the great') built on the intensive faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, established quality. The al- prefix means 'the'; the final -i is the genitive case, the form an adjective takes to agree with a genitive noun it describes.
18.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense (lit. related to 'bone', hence solidity/magnitude)

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: He plots, schemes, devises secretly — to work a hidden, cunning design against someone. The word is neutral in form (it can describe a stratagem for good or ill) but most often denotes covert scheming.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he plots'). The ya- prefix signals 'he.' The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action ('he plots / is plotting'), as opposed to the moods used in conditions or commands.
2.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — scheming, plotting, cunning stratagem

3.meaning: With You / in You — the preposition 'with/by/in' joined to the pronoun 'You' (addressing a single person), expressing reliance upon or recourse to that person.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/in/by') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', addressing one male). Pronouns following a preposition take this object form.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

6.meaning: So that they may hold you fast / confine you — to fix someone in place, restrain or imprison them, keeping them from moving. The 'li-' adds the purpose sense 'in order that.'

parts.en: make firm, hold fast, confine (form IV)

6.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they...'), on the causative pattern (form IV) meaning 'to make firm / hold fast.' The opening li- means 'so that / in order to' and puts the verb in the dependent mood, which is why the plural shows as -ū (without the usual final -na). The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you (one male).'
6.root: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t) — firmness, fixity; (form IV) making firm, confining

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: They kill you / put you to death — to slay, take the life of someone.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they kill'). The ya- prefix with the -ū ending signals the masculine plural 'they.' The absence of the final -na (so -ū not -ūna) shows a dependent mood, used after particles like 'or,' 'that,' or 'so that.' The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you (one male).'
8.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing, slaying, putting to death

9.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
9.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

10.meaning: They drive you out / expel you — to force someone to leave, to cast out from a place. The root means 'to bring/take out'; this causative form means 'to make go out, to banish.'

parts.en: bring out, expel, banish (causative form IV)

10.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they drive out'), on the causative pattern (form IV, with its yu- prefix) meaning 'to make someone go out.' The -ū ending marks the plural 'they'; the missing final -na signals a dependent mood after particles like 'or,' 'that,' or 'so that.' The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you (one male).'
10.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out; (form IV) bringing out, expelling

11.meaning: And they plot / scheme — the verb of devising a hidden, cunning design, stated of a group as an ongoing action.
11.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they plot'). The ya- prefix plus the full -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action. The retained final -na (unlike -ū alone) shows this is the independent indicative, not a dependent mood.

12.meaning: And He plots / devises — the same verb of cunning design, stated of a single 'He' as an ongoing action.
12.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he plots'). The ya- prefix signals 'he,' and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action.
12.root: م-ك-ر (m-k-r) — scheming, plotting, cunning stratagem

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
13.root: — (proper divine name)

14.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
14.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
14.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

15.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
15.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
15.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

16.meaning: The schemers / plotters — those who devise cunning, hidden designs. An active participle ('one who plots') made definite and plural.
16.grammar: An active participle ('plotter') with the definite article al- ('the'), masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the masculine plural in the object/genitive case — the form used when the word is the object of a verb or follows a preposition or another noun (as opposed to -ūna in the subject case).

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Our signs / verses — 'āyāt' are tokens, proofs, and miraculous indications that point to a deeper truth, and also the verses of revelation; with 'Our' it refers to such signs ascribed to Allah.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs, verses') with the attached possessive 'our' = -nā. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, the form a noun takes as the doer or topic of a sentence ('Our signs [are/do...]').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token, miraculous indication

5.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

6.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
6.root: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
7.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

8.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

9.meaning: We will, We so choose, We please — to will and desire a thing, exercising one's wish and choice. 'Shāʾa' denotes the act of willing that brings a matter about.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix marks the subject as 'we', and the final -u ending marks the plain, ongoing/habitual present ('we will', as a stated possibility or fact).
9.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing, choosing; the exercise of will

10.meaning: We surely said / we would certainly say — the verb 'to say' in the completed form for 'we,' with an emphatic 'la-' that stresses the certainty of the statement.
10.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb meaning 'to say,' with the attached subject ending -nā = 'we.' The opening la- is an emphatic particle ('surely, certainly') that strengthens the statement, often the response in 'if... then surely...' constructions. The middle vowel of the hollow root is dropped before the -nā ending (qul-nā).
10.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speaking, uttering

11.meaning: The like of / similar to; a match, equivalent, or counterpart — 'the same as' or 'something resembling.'
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'the like of.' The -a ending is the accusative case, the form typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — so it points to 'the like (of something)' as what is involved in the action.

12.meaning: This — a pointing word ('this one') used to single out something near at hand, masculine singular.
12.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, meaning 'this' — a word that points to a specific thing close by. It is a fixed, indeclinable word: its ending does not change for case, so it stays 'hādhā' whether it is subject, object, or follows a preposition.

13.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
13.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

14.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
14.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
15.root: — (particle)

16.meaning: "Legends, fables, written-down tales of old." Stories or accounts that have been set down and passed along — often with the nuance of mere old fables rather than authentic record.
16.grammar: A plural noun. The final -u ending marks the nominative case — the case a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being identified (as in "these are …"). Being the first term of a possessive phrase, it carries no indefinite tanwīn.
16.root: س-ط-ر (s-ṭ-r) — to write, draw lines, set down in rows

17.meaning: "The former ones, the people of old, the earlier generations." Those who came before, the ancients and predecessors.
17.grammar: A definite ("the") masculine plural noun/adjective. The "-īna" ending is the sound-masculine-plural form used in the accusative or genitive — i.e., when the word is an object, follows a preposition, or is linked to a preceding noun as its possessor ("… of the former ones").
17.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, foremost; beginning

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

3.meaning: O Allah — a vocative address to Allah. It is the divine name Allah with an added ending standing in place of the call-word 'O', so the whole word means 'O Allah' — an invocation calling directly upon Allah.
3.grammar: The proper name Allah used in direct address (vocative), with the suffixed -umma serving the function of the vocative 'O' that normally precedes a called noun. The word is fixed in this form for calling upon Allah ('O Allah').

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

5.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

6.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
6.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

7.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
7.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

8.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
8.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
8.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
9.root: — (preposition)

10.meaning: A noun of place/relation meaning 'at,' 'with,' 'in the presence of,' or 'in the keeping of' — denoting nearness, possession, or origin ('from where someone is'), here joined to 'you.'

parts.en: at / with / in the presence of

10.grammar: An adverbial noun of place that always governs a following genitive. The 'i' vowel on 'ʿindi' is the genitive linking vowel before the attached pronoun '-ka' ('you,' masculine singular), giving 'at/with you' — expressing presence, possession, or source.
10.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — nearness, being at hand, presence/proximity

11.meaning: Then rain down upon / send down (something) as rain — a command to cause something to fall from the sky like rain (often used of a downpour of punishment). The 'fa-' adds 'then / so.'

parts.en: rain down, send down as rain (causative form IV command)

11.grammar: A direct command (imperative) addressed to one person ('you, rain down!'), on the causative pattern (form IV) meaning 'to make rain fall.' The opening fa- means 'then / so.' The bare consonant ending (sukūn, no final vowel: amṭir) is the standard clipped form of a command.
11.root: م-ط-ر (m-ṭ-r) — rain; (form IV) to rain down, send down as rain

12.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
12.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

13.meaning: Stones; pieces of rock. This is the broken (irregular) plural of the singular noun ḥajar ('a stone'), denoting stones in the plural.
13.grammar: A feminine broken plural of ḥajar ('stone'), ending in tāʾ marbūṭa. It carries tanwīn fatḥa (the -an ending), the accusative case with 'nunation,' marking an indefinite noun ('stones / some stones') that typically functions as a direct object or specifier of quantity.
13.root: ح-ج-ر (ḥ-j-r) — stone, rock

14.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
14.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

15.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
15.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
15.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

16.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
16.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

17.meaning: 'Come!' (to more than one person, or with the sense 'come to us') — a command to approach or come forward. The base verb means to come or arrive.
17.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to someone, built on the verb 'to come.' Its initial vowel is a helping (connecting) vowel that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced. The attached -nā means 'us,' giving the sense 'come to us.'
17.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to bring

18.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
18.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

19.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
19.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: So that He may punish them / chastise them. A purpose construction built on a verb meaning to inflict severe, deliberate punishment or torment, intensified to convey repeated or thorough chastisement.
4.grammar: The prefix li- ('so that') puts the present-tense verb into the subjunctive, shown by the final -a on yuʿadhdhiba; it expresses purpose ('in order that…'). The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('He'), and the doubled middle letter marks the intensive form. The attached -hum means 'them' (masculine plural object).

5.meaning: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
5.grammar: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

6.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
6.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

8.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

8.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
9.root: — (proper divine name)

10.meaning: One who punishes them; the inflicter of their chastisement. An active participle naming the doer of intense, deliberate punishment.
10.grammar: An active participle ('one who…') from the intensive verb form: the mu- prefix and doubled middle letter mark the doer. The stem's final -a here reflects its case before the attached pronoun; the suffix -hum ('them') is the object of the participle, giving 'one who punishes them.'
10.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment

11.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
11.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

12.meaning: They seek forgiveness; they ask Allah to pardon and cover over their sins. Built on a verb meaning to actively request forgiveness.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the seeking/requesting form (the sta- pattern means 'to ask for' the root's sense). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine present tense; the plural 'they' comes from the ending -ūna, which marks third-person masculine plural and the indicative mood (a plain, ongoing statement, not yet altered by any governing particle).
12.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
3.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

4.meaning: That He may punish them / chastise them. A present-tense verb of intense, deliberate punishment with an attached object 'them.'
4.grammar: Present-tense verb in the intensive form (doubled middle letter), with yu- marking third-person masculine singular ('He'). The final -a is the subjunctive vowel, typical after a 'that/so that' particle expressing purpose or possibility. The attached -humu means 'them' (the -u is a connecting vowel before a following word).

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
6.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

7.meaning: they turn away / they bar (others) — to hold back, hinder, or avert; to turn oneself or others aside from something. The verb describes an ongoing, present action by a group.
7.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna (the -ū fused into the doubled d, written ṣuddūna) marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement ('they turn away'). The doubled d reflects the geminate root.
7.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, avert, hinder, bar

8.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

9.meaning: The place of prostration; a mosque — literally the spot where one bows down (sajda) in worship. With the following 'sacred', it names the Sacred Mosque.
9.grammar: A noun of place on the form mafʿil ('the place where prostration is done'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the possessed/qualified noun after another ('… OF the mosque').
9.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

10.meaning: The sacred, inviolable, forbidden; that which is set apart and protected, whose violation is prohibited out of reverence. Describes something hallowed.
10.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
10.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
12.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: Its guardians / protecting friends / patrons — those who stand close, ally with, and take charge of something. Plural of walī, a person bound to another by loyalty, protection, and nearness.
13.grammar: Broken plural of walī ('guardian, ally'). The -a ending is accusative, the case typically used for a direct object. The attached -hu ('its/his') is a possessive pronoun, giving 'its guardians.' Note this plural pattern does not take nunation.
13.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, allegiance, guardianship

14.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
14.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

15.meaning: Its guardians / protecting friends / patrons — those bound by loyalty and protection. Plural of walī, here in a form typically used as the subject.
15.grammar: Broken plural of walī. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject ('the guardians [do / are]…'). The attached -hu ('its/his') is a possessive pronoun. This plural pattern takes no nunation.
15.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, allegiance, guardianship

16.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
16.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

17.meaning: Those who have taqwā — the God-conscious, the mindful and dutiful. It describes people who keep a vigilant awareness of Allah, guarding themselves against wrongdoing and shielding themselves from His displeasure out of reverent care.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

17.grammar: The l- prefix is 'the'. This is an active participle (one who does the action). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the subject (nominative) form, i.e. the ones who carry out the guarding/mindfulness.
17.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield oneself

18.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
18.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

19.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'most of them / the greater part of them' — the larger portion of a group.
19.grammar: An elative/comparative noun ('more/most, the greater number') on the 'afʿal' pattern. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form used when the word is a verb's object. The attached -hum ('them') is in the possessive role, completing the sense 'the most of them'.

20.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
20.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

21.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
21.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

3.meaning: Their prayer / their formal worship. Ṣalāt denotes the prescribed act of devotion combining standing, bowing, prostration, and supplication before Allah.
3.grammar: A feminine noun (the underlying tāʾ appears as -t- before the suffix). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum ('their,' masculine plural) is possessive: 'their prayer.'

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

5.meaning: Al-bayt — the house, dwelling, or home; a place of residence or a building set apart, often used for a household or a place of worship.
5.grammar: A definite noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word denotes a house, dwelling, or set-apart sacred building.
5.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night; house, dwelling

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'

7.meaning: Whistling; producing a thin, shrill sound by blowing through the lips. A verbal noun naming the act of whistling.
7.grammar: A verbal noun (name of an action) ending in -an (tanwīn fatḥa): the accusative case with nunation, marking an indefinite noun that commonly serves as an object or as a descriptive complement ('as whistling').

8.meaning: And clapping / hand-clapping. A verbal noun for striking the palms together to produce sound, joined by 'and.'
8.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and,' linking this to a preceding item. The word is a verbal noun (name of an action) ending in -an (tanwīn fatḥa): accusative with nunation, marking an indefinite noun that typically acts as an object or descriptive complement.

9.meaning: So taste! — a command to a group to 'taste' or experience something, often used figuratively of undergoing a consequence or punishment.
