10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish; a standing group of people

11.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
11.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

12.meaning: A verb (Form II) meaning 'they change/alter' — to transform something from one state to another; Form II carries the active, causative sense of bringing about a change.
12.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural ('they ...'). The -ū plural ending without a final -na marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the clipped form used after certain particles (e.g. 'until', 'so that') or negations/conditions.
12.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — change, alteration, becoming other

13.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: 'Against / with themselves' or 'by means of themselves.' Combines the preposition bi- ('with/against/by') with 'anfus' ('selves, souls', the plural of nafs) and a possessive 'their'.
14.grammar: 'Anfus' is the broken plural of 'nafs' (self/soul). The preposition bi- governs the genitive case, shown by the -i vowel before the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The whole phrase functions adverbially ('with/against their own selves').
14.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; the inner being

15.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
15.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

17.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").
17.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen

18.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
18.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: Like the way / like the habitual practice (of someone). Daʾb means a settled custom, persistent habit, or characteristic manner of acting. With the prefixed particle of comparison it means 'like the manner/custom of …'.

parts.tr: daʾb (hamza often unwritten in transliteration as 'dab')

1.grammar: A noun preceded by the particle ka- ('like, as'). Because ka- functions like a preposition, the noun takes the -i (genitive) ending. The classical form has a hamza as its middle radical (dāl-hamza-bāʾ), so the careful pronunciation is 'daʾb' (full form ka-daʾb-i); simplified transliterations often drop the hamza and write it as 'dab' (ka-dab-i), but the hamza is a genuine sound of the word. The genitive is the case that follows prepositions and also links a noun to a following noun in a possessive sense ('the custom OF …').
1.root: د-أ-ب (d-ʾ-b) — to persist, toil habitually; hence a settled custom or habit

2.meaning: The family, folk, or close people of someone — those belonging to a person's household, following, or kin.
2.grammar: A singular collective noun in the genitive (-i ending), which typically links it to a following noun ('the folk OF …') or follows a preposition. It points to those associated with a named person.
2.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinsfolk (āl is derived from ahl by elision of the hāʾ)

3.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
3.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

4.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
6.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

7.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

8.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
8.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
8.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

9.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
9.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

10.meaning: 'So/then We destroyed them' — to annihilate, ruin, or cause to perish utterly. The verb ahlaka means to bring about destruction or doom, joined here to a connector 'so/then' and an object 'them.'
10.grammar: A causative (Form IV) past-tense verb meaning 'to cause to perish.' The -nā ending marks the subject 'we' (a completed act by a plural or majestic 'we'), and the attached -hum is the object 'them.' The fa- prefix means 'so/then,' showing sequence or consequence.
10.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed, come to ruin

11.meaning: For/because of their sins. Dhunūb is the plural of dhanb — a sin, fault, or offense; a wrongdoing that incurs blame. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'because of / for their sins'.
11.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi-, which here carries a causal sense ('because of, by reason of') and requires the -i (genitive) ending on the noun. The attached -him means 'their' (a group). The vowel of the pronoun is -him (rather than -hum) because it follows the -i sound.
11.root: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — to commit an offense; hence sin, fault

12.meaning: "and We drowned (something/someone)" — a past-tense verb of causing to sink and perish in water; the "We" is the majestic/plural divine subject.
12.grammar: Form-IV causative past-tense verb ("to make sink, to drown"). The attached -nā ending is the subject "we," marking a completed action done by a plural/majestic doer; the leading wa- is the connective "and."
12.root: غ-ر-ق (gh-r-q) — to sink, be submerged, drown

13.meaning: The 'house', family, kinsfolk, or followers of someone — those belonging to a person's household or close circle, including dependents and adherents.
13.grammar: A noun meaning the people/household belonging to someone. The '-a' ending is the accusative case (marking it as a direct object); as the first term of a possessive pairing it is typically followed by the name of the one whose folk they are ('the folk OF …').
13.root: Uncertain/contested: most classical grammarians (e.g. Sibawayh) treat it as a contraction of أَهْل (ʾ-h-l, 'folk, household'); others trace it to ء-و-ل (ʾ-w-l, 'to return to, belong to')

14.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
14.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

15.meaning: 'And all / and each / every one' — kull denotes totality or completeness: the whole of a group ('all') or every single member taken individually ('each one').
15.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The noun is indefinite and in the nominative case, the form used for a subject. The closing -un is nunation ('-un'); standing alone with nunation it carries the sense 'each one / all of them'.
15.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — all, whole, the totality, each

16.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
16.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: Those who do wrong — wrongdoers who put things out of their right place: unjust people, oppressors, and especially those who transgress against the truth and against the rights of Allah or of others. The root sense is placing something where it does not belong.
17.grammar: This is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used when the word is an object, or follows a preposition, or is linked to a preceding noun ('of the wrongdoers').
17.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, darkness

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: Worst, most evil, gravest in harm; or as a noun, evil/harm itself. From a root denoting wickedness and badness. In this comparative/superlative form it means 'more/most evil' or 'the worst of.'
2.grammar: A noun used in the superlative/comparative sense. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks a direct object, or appears when the word is the first term of a possessive 'X of Y' construct ('the worst of …').
2.root: ش-ر-ر (sh-r-r) — evil, wickedness, harm

3.meaning: The moving creatures, the beasts, all that crawls or treads the earth. From a root meaning 'to move / creep along,' a dābba is any living, moving animal; the plural covers the whole range of earthly creatures.
3.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun. The al- means 'the' (its l assimilates into the following d, written dd). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('the … of the creatures') or follows a preposition.
3.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move, creep, tread along

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

8.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
8.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.
10.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb (Form III) with an attached subject meaning 'you made a covenant / entered a pact' — to bind oneself with another in a mutual, reciprocal agreement or treaty.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the -ta suffix marking the second-person masculine singular subject: 'you made a covenant'. The action is viewed as completed. (The doubled t in the transliteration reflects the suffix joining the verb.)
2.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, binding agreement

3.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'they break', 'they undo', or 'they violate' — to undo or dissolve something firmly tied, especially to break a pledge, covenant, or binding agreement.
5.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The core sense is the undoing of something firmly bound, such as a covenant.
5.root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ) — to break, undo, unravel (a pact)

6.meaning: 'Their covenant / their pledge' — an ʿahd is a solemn binding commitment, promise, or treaty; with the attached pronoun it means that pledge as belonging to them.
6.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending on the noun is accusative, the form typically used when the word is the object of a verb. The -hum suffix means 'their' (masculine plural).
6.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, binding agreement

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

9.meaning: One time / once / an instance — a noun denoting a single occurrence of an act. Indefinite ('a time'), as shown by its two-vowel (tanwin) ending.
9.grammar: A feminine noun meaning 'a single time/occurrence'. The doubled-vowel ending (tanwin, here -in) marks it as indefinite ('a time', not 'the time'); the -i quality of that ending is genitive, signalling the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. It often expresses 'one time / once'.
9.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — passing by; an instance or occurrence of something

10.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
10.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.
10.root: — (conjunction plus pronoun; no root)

11.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

12.meaning: They are mindful of Allah / they guard themselves; to live in reverent awareness that shields one from wrongdoing (the verb behind taqwā).
12.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they (do)' for a group of males, with the final -na marking the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual reality.
12.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, shield, guard against harm

1.meaning: A compound conditional expression meaning 'then if ever' or 'so whenever'. It combines 'then/so' with a conditional 'if' to introduce a case that may arise, usually paired with a following emphasis on the verb.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so') joined to immā, itself the conditional particle 'in' ('if') merged with an emphasising mā. It sets up a condition — 'if it should happen that…' — and characteristically leads to a verb reinforced with a strong 'certainly' ending.

2.meaning: A verb with attached emphasis and object meaning 'you surely come upon / overtake / gain mastery over them' — to catch up with and get the better of someone, taking hold of them.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, second-person masculine singular ('you ...'), with the heavy emphatic ending -anna ('you most certainly will'), followed by the object pronoun -hum ('them', masculine plural). The doubled n is the emphasis marker.
2.root: ث-ق-ف (th-q-f) — to find, overtake, gain the upper hand over

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'The war / the fighting' — ḥarb denotes armed conflict, warfare, hostilities between opposing parties.
4.grammar: A definite singular noun. The al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it is the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').

5.meaning: A command (Form II) meaning 'scatter! / disperse! / drive away!' — to break up and put to flight, causing those addressed to scatter and flee in disarray.
5.grammar: Opens with fa- ('so / then'), linking it as a consequence to what precedes. The rest is a command (imperative) addressed to a single male ('you, scatter [them]!'). The bare final consonant (no ending vowel) is the normal close of such a singular command.
5.root: ش-ر-د (sh-r-d) — to scatter, disperse, drive off, make flee

6.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
6.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

7.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

8.meaning: 'behind them' — the space or position to the rear of a group; also figuratively what lies after them, what awaits them, or what is hidden from them.
8.grammar: An adverb of place ('behind') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The -a ending is accusative, the case regularly used for adverbs of place and time, indicating the location 'behind.'
8.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to be behind, come after, succeed

9.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

9.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
9.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

10.meaning: 'They take heed / call to mind' — to be reminded, to reflect and remember a lesson or truth, said of a group, in the present tense.
10.grammar: Present-tense reflexive verb (an assimilated form of 'yatadhakkarūna,' the self-reminding pattern). The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they'); '-ūna' is the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or repeated action.
10.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mention, mindfulness

1.meaning: And if (ever), and whenever. Combines 'and' with a conditional particle that introduces a possibility, often paired with an emphatic verb ('and should it ever happen that...').
1.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus immā, a conditional particle (the conditional 'in' fused with emphatic '-mā'). It sets up a hypothetical — 'and if it should ever be that...' — and frequently precedes a verb stressed with a heavy 'definitely' ending.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (certainly) fear' or 'you dread'. It carries the sense of apprehension or wariness toward a danger, and the heavy emphatic ending gives it the force of 'should you ever truly fear' or 'you surely fear'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb for a single 'you' (the ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject). The doubled-nūn ending (-anna), called the heavy nūn of emphasis (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla), is its own marker that strongly stresses the action — roughly 'you certainly do fear'. It is typically attached after a conditional particle or a command. The verb stem before the nūn is already in its base apocopate (jussive) shape with no separate final vowel, and the emphatic nūn is then added onto it; the nūn itself is not a subjunctive or jussive ending.
2.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, dread, apprehension

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: A people, folk, or community — a group of persons bound together (often by kinship or shared identity); a nation or tribe.
4.grammar: A singular collective noun (grammatically masculine, referring to a group). The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite ('a people'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of a people').
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish; a standing group of people

5.meaning: 'Betrayal, treachery, breach of trust'. It denotes the act of being faithless or disloyal — violating a covenant, trust, or confidence that was placed in someone.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -an ending (written with tanwīn on the closing tā') is the indefinite accusative: it marks the noun as 'a betrayal' functioning typically as a direct object of a verb or otherwise governed in the accusative case.
5.root: خ-و-ن (kh-w-n) — betrayal, breach of trust, treachery

6.meaning: 'So cast (it) back' or 'then throw (it) off / to them'. A command to fling or hurl something away or return it, often used figuratively for renouncing or repudiating an agreement openly.

parts.en: cast / throw back (command to one person)

6.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single 'you' (masculine singular). The leading fa- means 'so' or 'then', linking the order to what precedes (often the consequence of a condition). The verb ends in a silent/jussive form (sukūn on the last letter), which is the normal shape of a direct command.
6.root: ن-ب-ذ (n-b-dh) — to cast off, throw away, discard

7.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
7.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: 'Fair / equitable / common' — even-handed and just; something equal, level, or held in common between parties.
9.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective meaning 'equity, fairness, an even thing'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case — used after a preposition or to describe a preceding genitive noun ('a word that is fair'). It conveys evenness and impartiality.
9.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — evenness, equality, leveling

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
13.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

14.meaning: 'The betrayers / the treacherous ones' — those who habitually break trust or act with treachery. As an active participle it names the people characterised by committing betrayal.
14.grammar: A definite ('the') masculine plural active participle naming a group. The -īna ending is the 'sound masculine plural' in its accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — used when the plural is a direct object or follows a preposition or possessive link, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'he surely thinks/reckons' or 'let (him) by no means suppose' — to reckon, calculate, or be of the opinion; the doubled ending adds heavy emphasis, often used in solemn warnings.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), carrying the heavy 'nūn of emphasis' (-anna) suffix, which strongly stresses the action and is common after commands and prohibitions ('let him by no means …'). The 'ya-' prefix marks the subject.
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, reckon, calculate, suppose

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'They got ahead / outstripped / went before'. The verb conveys preceding others, racing ahead, or escaping beyond reach — getting away so as not to be overtaken.
5.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending (with a silent 'alif written after it) marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they' did the action. It signals an act viewed as finished or accomplished.
5.root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q) — to precede, outstrip, get ahead

6.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
6.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: 'They render (someone) powerless / frustrate / escape'. From a causative verb meaning to make another incapable — to outmatch, thwart, or elude so that the pursuer cannot prevail.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (af'ala) pattern, literally 'to render incapable'. The yu- prefix plus the -ūna ending together mark a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its base (indicative) mood, describing an ongoing or general action.

1.meaning: 'And prepare / make ready / muster'. A command to assemble and equip something in readiness, gathering resources and getting fully set for what is to come.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all', masculine plural), prefixed with wa- ('and'). The stem aʿidd carries the order, and the -ū ending (written with a silent 'alif) directs it to many people. The verb is of the causative (af'ala) pattern, giving the sense of actively getting things ready.
1.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, numbering; preparing, making ready

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
3.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

4.meaning: 'You were able / had the capacity / could manage'. From a verb meaning to be capable of something, to have the power or means to do it.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb in the 'seeking/striving' (istaf'ala) pattern, conveying mustering one's ability. The -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject — 'you all' did or could do it.
4.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — willing obedience, capability, being able

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: 'Strength, power, force, might'. It denotes capability and vigour — physical, military, or moral power, and the means by which one is strong.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -in ending (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive: it marks 'strength' as indefinite and in the genitive case, typically because it follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive/'of' link.
6.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — strength, power, might

7.meaning: And from / and out of — the conjunction 'and' joined to the preposition 'from', expressing origin, source, starting-point, or 'some of'.
7.grammar: A compound particle: the connector 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the preposition 'min' ('from'). 'Min' governs a following noun in the genitive case and conveys starting-point, source, or partition ('some of').

8.meaning: 'Tethering / tying up', specifically the keeping and stationing of horses ready for action; also the bond or stationing at a frontier. It evokes binding fast and holding in readiness.
8.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action of tying/stationing). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links this word to a following noun in an 'of' relationship, or marks it as following a preposition.
8.root: ر-ب-ط (r-b-ṭ) — to tie, bind, tether; to station fast

9.meaning: 'Horses / horsemen / cavalry'. A collective noun denoting horses, especially as a body of steeds, with the extended sense of mounted fighters.
9.grammar: A definite ('the') collective noun referring to horses as a group. The -i ending is genitive: it shows the noun is the second term of a possessive/'of' link with a preceding noun, or that it follows a preposition.
9.root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l) — horses; also notions of pride/prancing

10.meaning: 'You strike fear into / overawe / deter'. From a causative verb meaning to make others dread — to intimidate or hold an adversary in check through fear.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (af'ala) pattern ('to cause to dread'). The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The full -ūna ending puts the verb in its base (indicative) mood, describing an ongoing or purposed action.
10.root: ر-ه-ب (r-h-b) — fear, dread, awe

11.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
11.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

12.meaning: 'Enemy, foe, adversary' — one who bears hostility and opposition. The word denotes an opponent set against you, whether an individual or a collective enemy.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -a ending is the accusative: it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or otherwise governed in the accusative. (The same form serves for singular and collective 'enemy'.)
12.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — enmity, hostility, transgression

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: 'And your enemy / your foe'. The base word means an adversary or opponent; with the attached 'your', it names the enemy belonging to or opposed to a group of people.
14.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -kum ('your', for a group of you, masculine plural) marking possession. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as a direct object or otherwise governed in the accusative.

15.meaning: 'And others / other ones'. The plural of 'another', denoting additional persons distinct from those already mentioned — a further group besides them.
15.grammar: A masculine plural noun/adjective meaning 'others', prefixed with wa- ('and'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — used when the word is a direct object or follows a preposition, rather than the -ūna subject form.
15.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, otherness

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: 'Apart from them / besides them / below them'. The base word 'dūn' marks something other than or short of a reference point; with 'them' attached it means 'other than those people' or 'lower/nearer than them'.

parts.en: genitive ending (after this word, before the pronoun)

17.grammar: An adverb/preposition of relation ('apart from, besides, short of') with the attached pronoun -him ('them', masculine plural). The -i vowel is the genitive linking the word to the pronoun; the form -him (with i-vowel) is the regular shape the pronoun takes after a genitive/'i' sound.
17.root: — (function word; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

19.meaning: 'You know them / you recognise them'. From the verb 'to know', with an attached object 'them' — to have knowledge or awareness of those persons.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix and -ūna ending marking a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), in its base (indicative) mood for an ongoing or general action. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them'; its final vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following sound.

20.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole and absolute Deity worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a name, not a common noun, and refers to the Creator and Sustainer of all that exists.
20.grammar: The proper divine name. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject (the doer) of a sentence or the noun being identified.

21.meaning: 'He knows them / He recognises them'. From the verb 'to know', with attached 'them' — having full knowledge or awareness of those persons.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The -u ending is the base (indicative) mood, used for an ongoing or habitual action. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them'.

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
22.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

23.meaning: You spend, expend, or give out — to lay out wealth or resources, especially in charity or for a cause; the act of disbursing what one has rather than withholding it.
23.grammar: Present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The tu- prefix marks the present tense and the 'you' subject; the -ū ending marks a plural ('you all') subject. The form lacks the final -na of the plain indicative, signalling a 'dependent' mood — the form a verb takes after certain particles (such as those meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or in conditional 'if' clauses). It comes from form IV (causative), 'to make wealth go forth,' i.e. to spend.
23.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, to expend, to disburse

24.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
24.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

25.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
25.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
25.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

26.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
26.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

27.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
27.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

28.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
28.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

29.meaning: 'It is paid back in full / repaid completely'. From a passive verb meaning to be given one's due fully and without shortfall — to be recompensed in entirety.
29.grammar: A present-tense passive verb in the intensive (faʿʿala) pattern, conveying 'rendered in full'. The yu- prefix with the a-vowel pattern marks it as passive ('is repaid') for a third-person masculine singular subject. The final -a is the subjunctive/jussive shortened ending — the verb stands in a dependent (non-indicative) mood, its weak final letter dropped so only -a remains.
29.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, paying in full, keeping faith

30.meaning: To you / toward you (plural) — a preposition expressing motion or direction reaching a destination, joined with 'you all' as that destination.
30.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, toward'), whose ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached, plus -kum ('you all'). Together they mark the end-point or recipient of an action — the direction 'toward' or 'unto' a group.

31.meaning: And you / while you (all) — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), often introducing an accompanying circumstance ('while you …').
31.grammar: The conjunction wa- joined to the detached subject pronoun 'you all' (masculine). This standalone pronoun stands as a subject or for emphasis; it has a fixed form and does not change for case. With wa- it can mark a simultaneous state ('and you / while you').

32.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
32.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

33.meaning: You are wronged / treated unjustly — to have injustice done to one, to be deprived of a right or given less than one's due; the passive of doing wrong or oppression.
33.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all are …'). The tu- prefix with this vowel pattern marks the passive and the 'you' subject; the -ūna ending marks a plural subject and the indicative mood — the plain factual form stating something that happens or will happen. Passive voice means the people receive the action ('are wronged') rather than do it.
33.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, to do injustice, oppression

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'They inclined / leaned toward'. The verb conveys bending or tilting in a direction — figuratively, being disposed or favourably inclined toward something.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending (with silent 'alif written after) marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). It presents the action as finished or accomplished.
2.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, bend toward (also: wing, side)

3.meaning: 'Toward peace / for reconciliation'. The base word 'salm' means peace, making-up, or reconciliation — the laying-down of hostility; with the prefix it means 'to/for peace'.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the peace') carrying the prefixes li- ('to/for') and the assimilated 'the' (al- becoming -ssa- before the sun-letter s). The -i ending is genitive, which is the case a noun takes after the preposition li-.

4.meaning: 'So incline / then lean toward (it)'. A command to bend or be disposed in a direction — figuratively, to be willing and favourably inclined toward something.

parts.en: incline / lean toward (command to one person)

4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single 'you' (masculine singular), prefixed with fa- ('so/then') linking it to a preceding clause (often a condition's result). The verb ends in a silent final letter (sukūn), the normal form of a direct command.
4.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, bend toward

5.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
5.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

6.meaning: And rely / and place your trust. A command (singular 'you') to entrust one's affairs fully to another and depend on Him completely, with calm reliance.
6.grammar: A masculine-singular command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'you, rely!'. It comes from a Form V verb pattern (tafaʿʿala) that conveys taking something fully upon oneself — here, deliberately committing one's reliance to another. The vowel-less ending (sukūn) is the normal final state of an imperative.
6.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

7.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
7.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
7.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
9.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

10.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

11.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
11.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

12.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
12.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
12.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'They intend / want / desire / aim at'. From a verb meaning to will or purpose something — to set one's intention toward a goal.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (af'ala) pattern meaning 'to will/intend'. The yu- prefix with the -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). Here the plural lacks the final -na (giving -ū rather than -ūna), which signals the subjunctive/jussive mood — the verb being governed by a preceding particle.
2.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, will; to go to and fro in pursuit

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'They deceive you / trick you'. From a verb meaning to delude or beguile through deceit — to mislead by trickery; with attached 'you' it targets a single addressee.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix and -ū plural marker giving a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The plural lacks the final -na (giving -ū rather than -ūna), signalling the subjunctive/jussive mood under a governing particle. The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (a single masculine addressee).

5.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
5.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

6.meaning: A statement that someone or something is enough, adequate, and a sufficing support — 'enough for you,' carrying the sense that nothing more is needed once this is present.
6.grammar: A noun meaning 'an enough/a sufficiency' in a possessive construct (iḍāfa) with the attached pronoun -ka ('you,' masculine singular). The pronoun is the possessor ('your'), giving the reading 'your sufficiency = enough for you.' The -a ending is the accusative case, which the noun takes from its own role in the sentence; the attached pronoun does not cause this vowel — a construct noun keeps whatever case its position assigns. The attached -ka marks a single male addressee.
6.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, suffice

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
8.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

9.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

10.meaning: To strengthen, reinforce, and back someone up with aid — to lend support so that a person becomes firm and powerful.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb (intensive form II) in the third-person masculine singular: 'he supported/reinforced.' The fixed -a ending on the verb stem marks completed past action by a single male doer, and the attached -ka ('you,' masculine singular) is the object — the one who was supported.
10.root: ا-ي-د (ʾ-y-d) — strength, support, reinforcement

11.meaning: 'with His help / aid / victory' — the noun for divinely granted help or victory, governed by 'with/by' and joined to the pronoun 'His.'
11.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by means of') + the verbal noun naṣr ('help, support, victory') + the possessive pronoun -hi ('his/its'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending required after the preposition bi-. Naṣr denotes the granting of aid that brings triumph; when the pronoun refers to Allah it means 'with Allah's help.'

12.meaning: 'And with the believers' — those who have faith and trust, made the joined-on object of a 'with/by means of' relationship.
12.grammar: Connector wa ('and') plus the preposition bi ('with/by'), then the definite plural noun 'the believers.' The form is the sound masculine plural; its ending -īna is the oblique (genitive/accusative) case, which is what the preposition bi requires — so the whole word reads 'and with the believers.' 'Believers' here is an active participle: those who actively have faith.
12.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, faith, trust

1.meaning: 'And He brought into harmony / joined in affection' — to unite hearts, knit people together, and create loving accord between them.
1.grammar: Connector wa ('and') plus a past-tense verb (form II) in the third-person masculine singular: 'he joined together / reconciled hearts.' The -a ending marks completed past action by a single male doer.
1.root: ا-ل-ف (ʾ-l-f) — to join, unite, bring into familiarity/affection

2.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
2.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
2.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

3.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
3.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
3.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

4.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

5.meaning: 'You spent / expended' — to lay out and give away wealth or resources, putting them forth for some purpose.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV) with the subject ending -ta, which marks the doer as 'you' (a single male addressee) who completed the action: 'you spent.' The -ta suffix is the second-person singular past-tense marker.

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
8.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

9.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.
9.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining, bringing together

10.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
10.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
10.root: — (particle; no root)

11.meaning: 'You joined / united in affection' — that you (yourself) could have brought hearts together into loving accord.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb (form II) with the subject ending -ta marking the doer as 'you' (a single male addressee) who completed the action: 'you united (hearts).' The -ta suffix is the second-person masculine singular past-tense marker.
11.root: ا-ل-ف (ʾ-l-f) — to join, unite, bring into familiarity/affection

12.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
12.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
12.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

13.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
13.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
13.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

14.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
14.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
15.root: — (proper name)

16.meaning: 'He joined / united in affection' — to knit hearts together and create loving harmony between people.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb (form II) in the third-person masculine singular. The -a ending marks completed past action by a single male doer: 'he brought (them) together in affection.'
16.root: ا-ل-ف (ʾ-l-f) — to join, unite, bring into familiarity/affection

17.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
17.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
17.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

18.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
18.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

19.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
19.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

20.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
20.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
20.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
2.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

3.meaning: A statement that someone or something is enough and fully sufficing — 'enough for you,' such that no further support is needed.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'an enough/a sufficiency' in a possessive construct (iḍāfa) with the pronoun -ka ('you,' masculine singular) as the possessor ('your sufficiency = enough for you'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which the noun takes from its own role as the subject or starting point of a sentence; the attached pronoun does not cause this vowel. The attached -ka marks a single male addressee.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: And whoever / and the one who: 'and' joined to a word meaning 'who(ever)' — referring to a person or persons, often introducing a condition ('whoever does…') or a relative clause ('the one who…').
5.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the pronoun 'man' ('who / whoever'), which refers to people. 'man' itself does not change for case; the final -i is only a helping vowel added to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting before the next word.

6.meaning: 'Followed you / went after you' — to follow behind, adhere to, and take as one's lead or example.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) in the third-person masculine singular: 'he followed.' The -a ending marks completed past action by a single male doer, and the attached -ka ('you,' masculine singular) is the object — the one who is followed.
6.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue
