42.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
42.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
42.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

43.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
43.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

44.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
44.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
44.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

45.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
45.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

3.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
3.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
3.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

4.meaning: Protectors, close allies, guardians, intimate friends — those bound to one another in loyalty, support, and mutual responsibility. A 'walī' is one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs; the plural gathers many such allies.
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of walī. The final -u is the nominative ending, the state a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (as in 'they are allies').

5.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
5.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
5.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: You (plural) do it / would do it — the general verb 'to do, make, act, carry out,' with 'it' as the object of the action.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to 'you all,' with attached object 'it.' The plural-marking 'nūn' that would normally end such a verb has dropped (leaving '-ū' + 'hu'), which signals the jussive/subjunctive mood — the form used after a conditional 'if…' or a negation.

8.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: A trial, test, or temptation; affliction or seduction that puts faith and character to the proof and may lead one into discord or sin.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the -ah/-at ending) in the nominative case. The -un ending pairs the nominative marker -u (subject / predicate form) with nunation (-n), marking it indefinite: 'a trial'.
9.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire, try; trial, temptation

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
10.root: — (particle)

11.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
11.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

12.meaning: And corruption, ruin, spoilage, disorder — the marring of what is sound and the spread of mischief and decay, the opposite of wholesome order and rightness. Joined by 'and.'
12.grammar: 'wa-' ('and') + an indefinite verbal noun. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks the nominative case — the form for the subject of a sentence or a thing being named/stated to exist — and the 'un' sound shows it is indefinite ('corruption / a corruption').
12.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoiled, ruined

13.meaning: Great, big, grave, weighty — large in size, importance, or seriousness.
13.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern conveying an intense, established quality ('great'). The final -un (nominative with nunation) marks it as indefinite and as a predicate or describing word ('is great'), not an object.
13.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: And they emigrated — they migrated, departing from their homes and severing ties for a cause; the verb carries the sense of forsaking one place and people to go to another. Joined by 'and.'
3.grammar: 'wa-' ('and') + a past-tense verb in the mutual/effortful (fāʿala) form, with the subject ending '-ū' meaning 'they' did it. It reports a completed migration.

4.meaning: They struggled, strove, and exerted earnest effort, expending energy and capability against hardship or opposition. The verb carries the sense of striving with one's wealth and self toward a goal, often the cause of Allah, and is the source of the well-known term jihad. The doubled, lengthened pattern conveys mutual, sustained, strenuous exertion.
4.grammar: A completed-action (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (men, or a mixed group) did' the action. The form jāhada (with the long ā after the first root letter) is the pattern of mutual or intensive effort: striving strenuously against something. The prefixed wa simply means 'and', joining this to what precedes.
4.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to exert effort, strive, struggle

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
6.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

9.meaning: They gave shelter, took in, and granted refuge, providing a safe lodging or haven to someone, drawing them in and offering protection and a place to stay. The verb also bears the sense of giving someone a home or harboring them.

parts.en: he gave shelter / took in (Form IV stem)
they (masculine plural), with silent final alif

9.grammar: A completed-action (perfect) verb in the fourth (causative) pattern, meaning 'to cause to find shelter / to give refuge'. It is a defective (nāqiṣ) verb whose final root letter is wāw, so its third-person masculine plural perfect ending is -aw (written وْا), not the regular -ū. The wāw of this ending carries the 'aw' sound and is followed by a silent orthographic alif. The form indicates the action was fully carried out: 'they sheltered / they took in'.
9.root: ا-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to seek shelter, take refuge, find a lodging

10.meaning: And they helped, aided, supported, and gave victory — to come to someone's aid against an opponent and make them prevail. Joined by 'and.'
10.grammar: 'wa-' ('and') + a past-tense verb with the subject ending '-ū' meaning 'they' did it. It reports a completed act of helping.
10.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

11.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
11.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

12.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
12.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

13.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
13.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).
13.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust, faith

14.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
14.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
14.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

15.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
15.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

16.meaning: Forgiveness — Allah's covering over and pardoning of sins; the act and gift of having one's faults effaced.
16.grammar: A verbal noun of the 'mafʿila' pattern, naming the abstract action of forgiving. The '-tun' ending combines the feminine '-t-' with '-un', the nominative-indefinite marker, which typically marks an indefinite subject ('a forgiveness') — the one acting or being asserted to exist.

17.meaning: And a provision — sustenance, livelihood, or that which is bestowed for one's needs, whether food, wealth, or any granted good. The root points to whatever a provider supplies for living.
17.grammar: A noun naming a thing provided. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative ('tanwīn'): it typically marks an indefinite noun as the subject or as something asserted to exist ('a provision'). Prefixed wa- means 'and'.
17.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, bestow sustenance; the livelihood granted by a provider.

18.meaning: Noble, generous, honourable, and precious. Describes that which is held in high esteem, abundant in goodness, and free of meanness — applied to things prized and to a giving, magnanimous character.
18.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying an abundant, settled quality). The -un ending is the indefinite nominative ('tanwīn'): it commonly marks an indefinite word as subject or as a description asserted of something.
18.root: ك-ر-م (k-r-m) — nobility, generosity, honour; being precious and abundant in good.

1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: After; afterward, subsequent in time or sequence. It points to what comes following something else. In this particular vowel-form it stands on its own as 'afterward' without naming what it comes after.
4.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u here is a fixed ending taken when the word is used absolutely ('afterward'), with the thing it follows understood rather than stated, rather than being linked to a following noun.

5.meaning: And they emigrated — they migrated, departing from their homes and severing ties for a cause; the verb carries the sense of forsaking one place and people to go to another. Joined by 'and.'
5.grammar: 'wa-' ('and') + a past-tense verb in the mutual/effortful (fāʿala) form, with the subject ending '-ū' meaning 'they' did it. It reports a completed migration.

6.meaning: And they strove / struggled / exerted themselves — they put forth utmost effort and struggled, including in the way of Allah.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb of the mutual/effortful (form III) pattern, 'to exert utmost effort / struggle against'. The -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural) as the doers of a completed action. (The written final alif is a silent spelling convention.)
6.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — exertion, striving, struggle

7.meaning: An expression meaning 'with you' — combining the word for accompaniment, togetherness, or presence-alongside with the attached pronoun 'you' (a group). It signals being in the company of, or on the side of, the addressed people.
7.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with/in the company of') carrying the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' for a group of males). It expresses togetherness or being alongside the people addressed.

8.meaning: A pointing word meaning 'those' — used to indicate a group already mentioned or in view, often emphatically singling them out as 'those very ones'.
8.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so/then', often introducing a result. The remainder is a demonstrative pronoun, 'those', pointing to a plural group at a distance. Demonstratives of this kind are fixed in form and do not change for case; the final -ka is an intrinsic deictic element of the pronoun itself, not a separable suffix.

9.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
9.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
9.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

10.meaning: And those possessing — 'and the owners/holders of …', a plural construct meaning 'people endowed with' or 'masters of' whatever follows. 'Ulū' has no singular of its own form and always leads into a following noun.
10.grammar: A masculine plural noun meaning 'possessors/owners of', preceded by 'wa' ('and'). It exists only in a possessive ('… of …') construction and must be followed by another noun naming what is possessed. The '-ū' ending is the masculine plural form used for a subject; in this bound state it has dropped its final 'n', linking it to the following noun.
10.root: — (a plural noun used only in construct; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: The wombs; by extension, ties of kinship and blood relationship. The plural of the noun for the womb, often evoking the bonds among relatives.
11.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun on the afʿāl pattern, made definite by the article al-. The final -i ending is genitive, the case typically used after a preposition, after an oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

12.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
12.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
12.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

13.meaning: More entitled, more deserving, closer in claim or priority. A comparative meaning 'worthier (of)' or 'having a stronger right (to)'.
13.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) adjective on the pattern afʿalu, expressing 'more X' or 'most X'. It is invariable in this spelling, ending in a long final ā, and is typically followed by 'than' or by the thing one has a claim to.
13.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance, guardianship, priority

14.meaning: 'In part / in some' — referring to a portion or some of a whole, here left indefinite. The bi- prefix gives the sense of disbelieving 'in' something.
14.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with') plus the noun baʿḍ ('a part, some'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr) is the genitive case with indefiniteness, required after bi- and marking the noun as 'some (unspecified) part.'
14.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
15.root: — (particle)

16.meaning: A scripture or book; in particular a written revelation. The word denotes something written down and consigned to record — a 'Book' in the sense of a divinely sent, recorded scripture, also carrying the broader sense of a binding decree or anything set down in writing.
16.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -i ending is genitive (the 'of' case): it typically marks the word as linked to a following noun ('… OF …'), or as governed by a preceding preposition or oath particle.

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
18.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
20.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').
